How close two vertices may be before they can merge, in model units. Higher values can change the shape. Zero requires identical positions.
How close texture coordinates may be before vertices can merge. Higher values can shift texture details. Zero preserves exact texture coordinates.
The largest difference between surface directions that may merge. Higher angles can soften sharp edges. Zero requires identical normals.
Merge bones with identical transforms, pivots and parents when they have no children. Vertices keep the same movement.

Maximum sampled movement difference, in model units. Small motions and turning poses also have a 10% relative limit; keys are kept when reduction would exceed it. Zero removes only proven redundant keys.
Maximum sampled rotation difference, in degrees. Curved tracks are supported. Small rotations and turning poses also have a 10% relative limit, preserving motion even at high settings.
Maximum sampled scale difference. A value of 0.01 is about one percent on one axis. Each axis and turning pose also has a 10% relative motion limit, so small scale cycles stay animated.
Delete vertices that no triangle uses, along with bone groups that no remaining vertex uses. Excluded geosets are preserved.
The triangle count to aim for. Lower values remove more detail. Protection settings may prevent reaching this number.
How much shape and texture deviation the polygon reducer may accept. Higher values allow more reduction; inspect the silhouette and texture details.

MDX saves the binary model. MDL saves editable text. Both preserve supported model data; unsupported conversion is blocked before writing.

Default Hotkeys (customize in Settings): F1 vertices · F2 selected UV maps · F3 Movement. Bones edits the unanimated rig. Animations edits visibility and RGB; BAKE applies current visibility and RGB across the selected animation; ALL applies them across every animation. Bake Text applies edited text tracks. A select · M/Q move · R rotate · Z scale. W switches between work and camera rotation. F toggles Textured View on and off; S selects Surface. Wireframe remains available beside the view direction. Use View / Fit to frame the model.
Geoset checkboxes control which meshes can be selected. Only checkboxes change selection; Shift checks a range. All, Clear and Invert act on the geoset list. Hide/Show affects editor visibility only.

T creates a triangle from three selected points. U uncouples, C collapses and B welds points. Welding retains the last selected vertex's UVs and binding. Copy remains available after opening another model.
Windows opens the material, texture, node and camera managers. Changes can be undone. Untouched saves preserve original bytes; edited sections regenerate through the codec.
Based on the original 1.41 form layout, with integrated material/node editing and recoverable undo history. The original application is unchanged.
